_about: measured quantization degradation, per model. SOURCE, not derived: nothing
in this repo can compute it, because it takes running the same model at two
or more quants on the same benchmark at the same settings.
MOSTLY EMPTY, and for a reason. the sweeps that exist here cannot fill it:
quantbench has 1269 scored trials across 15 configs, but only two models were
run at more than one quant and in both cases one arm has n<=2. a curve fitted
to that would be noise wearing a decimal point. what is here is published by
somebody who ran it.
a point is [bits per weight, retention], where retention is the score at
that quant over the score at the highest-precision arm of the SAME sweep --
same model, same benchmark, same samplers, same thinking level. anything
else is comparing two different measurements and calling the difference
quantization.
A SWEEP MEASURES FILES, NOT A MODEL, so `curves[model]` is a LIST and every
entry names the `quant_repo` it ran. ISTA-DASLab scored their own GSQ-RCO
rungs of qwen3.8 27b and unsloth's UD rungs on the same three benchmarks and
the two differ by more than eight points of task average at 2.5 bpw -- so
there is no such thing as the curve for that model, and the page applies a
curve only to a rung out of the repo it was run on. one score curve per
(model, quant_repo): a second measurement of the same files belongs in the
note, where it can be read against the first rather than silently preferred.
what a usable entry looks like:
"deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731": [{
"kind": "score",
"quant_repo": "unsloth/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-GGUF",
"metric": "aider polyglot pass rate",
"trials": 580,
"ref": {"source": "unsloth", "url": "https://...", "captured": "2026-08-17"}
scripts/build-viewer validates these on the way through: bits per weight
ascending, retention in (0, 1], at least two points, and a `quant_repo` on
every score curve. where a model has no entry the page falls back to the
median of the models that do have one, and to build-tables' fitted curve
when fewer than MIN_CURVES models do. the page says which of the three it
used, every time.
bits per weight are FILE SIZE over total parameters, which is what the page
interpolates against. where a card states a bpw over the transformer weights
alone -- as ISTA's flash-next card does, holding the n-gram table out of the
search -- its figure is not that measure and is not what is written here.

Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B.metric: mean of 14 benchmarks in THINKING mode, six skill categories

ref.note: prism benchmarked four builds of Qwen3.8-27B against each other to place their own ternary model, which makes it a sweep of SOMEBODY ELSE'S quants -- the only one here not published by the quantizer. EvalScope + vLLM on an H100, identical decoding and scoring, in thinking mode, 14 benchmarks. FP16 averages 86.32 and UD-Q4_K_XL 85.18, so 0.9868. THE THIRD ARM IS NOT RECORDED AS A POINT: an IQ2_XXS build at 2.8 bpw averaged 72.59, which is 0.8409 and by far the most interesting number here, but the card never says whose IQ2_XXS it is. a retention point whose FILE is unknown cannot be joined to a rung, which is what a point is for. it is kept in prose so the figure is not lost. that arm is also the sharpest published statement of how low-bit builds fail: it holds 88.93 on mmlu-redux while falling to 57.5 on aime26 and 56.4 on livecodebench, so a casual test reads fine and a reasoning chain does not. this sweep is the evidence behind the `native_low_bpw` exemption -- at a LOWER 1.72 bpw the natively-ternary bonsai 2 holds 0.982, against 0.841 for a conventional build at 2.8, which is the difference between weights trained to ternary and weights reduced to it

Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B.metric: task average over aime25, gpqa-diamond and livecodebench v6

ref.note: the publisher benchmarked their own rungs and printed the table: aime25, gpqa-diamond and livecodebench v6 against the bf16 base, whose task average is 91.87. retention here is the mean of those three over that, so IQ3_S at 91.70 is 0.9981 -- task-lossless on two of the three and 0.51 down on the third. THE SAME SWEEP RAN UNSLOTH'S RUNGS, which is the only published comparison of two quant families under one harness, and it is why this file keys on the repo: UD-IQ2_S lands at 0.8524 where GSQ-RCO's 2.43 bpw rung is 0.9364, UD-Q2_K_XL at 0.9766, UD-IQ3_S at 0.9817. those three are NOT points here because they are another repo's files; they are the reason a curve may not be lent to one. bits per weight are the file bytes over 27.78b parameters, so they read a little under the card's own column, which excludes nothing but rounds.

Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B.metric: terminal-bench 2.1 pass rate, 89 tasks, xhigh effort, 3h timeout

ref.note: READ FROM A CHART. the article publishes its results as graphs and prose and prints no score for any arm, so these retentions are the midpoints of what it states verbally -- bf16 and Q4_K_M both at about 78% pass, UD-Q2_K_XL at about 70-71%. the FILE SIZES it prints are exact (55 / 17 / 10.7 GB against bf16) and the bits per weight are derived from them. treat the shape as measured and the third decimal as decoration. the same sweep ran GPQA diamond across five arms including UD-IQ1_S at 1.80 bpw, where it collapsed to roughly random guessing -- the only BENCHMARK anybody has published below two bits, and it is NOT in these points, because mixing two benchmarks in one curve is the thing this file's schema forbids. it bounds what the curve below 3.11 bpw can claim rather than filling it in. byteshape has since published kl divergence over the same repo's ladder down to 1.78 bpw, which is the proxy entry below: a different measure, agreeing on the direction.

Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B.metric: quality relative to bf16, averaged over six suites in thinking and instruct modes

ref.note: FIVE QUANT FAMILIES UNDER ONE HARNESS, which is the widest published comparison this file holds -- byteshape's own ladder plus unsloth's twelve rungs, ISTA-DASLab's four, bartowski's six and AtomicChat's five, every one of them scored against the same bf16 reference and reported per gpu. only byteshape's own rungs are points here, because the other four are other repos' files and the two this roster already curves are already keyed: the sweep is a SECOND measurement of them and belongs where it can be read against the first. where it overlaps ISTA's own card it corroborates the part that matters -- ISTA's harness put unsloth's UD-IQ2_S at 0.8524 and this one puts it at 0.8633, two independent runs agreeing that unsloth's 2.4 bpw rung gives up about fifteen points where both publishers' own rungs at the same size give up six. it disagrees about the middle of ISTA's ladder, 0.9438 here against 0.9922 on ISTA's card for IQ3_XXS, which is what two different benchmark suites look like and why neither is allowed to overwrite the other. the scores are the card's 'Acc' column and are identical across all six gpu tables; only throughput moves. bits per weight are the file bytes over 27.78b parameters rather than the blog's own column, which is over the language weights alone and reads about 0.06 higher.

MEASURED BY A COMPETITOR RATHER THAN THE PUBLISHER, which is unusual here and is why the repo it measures is named rather than assumed: every other proxy in this file is a card reporting its own work. twenty-four rungs of unsloth's ladder, and the only evidence anybody has published below two bits for this model other than quesma's GPQA arm -- UD-IQ1_S at 1.78 bpw diverges 0.39, which is 600x the Q8_0 rung and 77x its own UD-Q4_K_XL. the two rungs that are not UD are where the ladder stops being monotonic: Q4_0 at 4.62 bpw diverges more than UD-Q4_K_S below it and more than twice UD-Q4_K_M above it, and Q4_1 the same, which is the dynamic allocation doing its job and is visible only because this sweep ran the plain rungs too. a kl divergence is not comparable to another card's and is shown rather than applied, so this discounts nothing.

Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next.metric: task average over aime25, gpqa-diamond and livecodebench v6

ref.note: the same three benchmarks against a bf16 base whose task average is 93.12, so IQ3_XXS at 92.57 is 0.9941. the two rungs below it land within a tenth of a point of each other on task average by different routes -- Q2_0 is ahead on gpqa-diamond and behind on livecodebench v6 -- which is why the curve is nearly flat under 3.1 bpw rather than falling. bits per weight are the download bytes over 180b parameters, INCLUDING the n-gram shard, which the card's own bpw column excludes: its 2.40 for Q2_0 is over the transformer weights the search controls, and the 2.95 here is the whole file, which is what the page interpolates against. the unsloth proxy beside this entry is kl divergence on another repo's files and the two cannot be read against each other.
